journeyStory.heading: A Defining Moment in Civilization
paragraphs: In 2026, we stand at a defining moment in human civilization.
Artificial intelligence, digital technologies, and global connectivity are transforming our world at an unprecedented pace.
They are changing more than the tools we use. They are reshaping how we work, learn, communicate, build relationships, and even how we understand truth, human identity, and the future.
Yet the more powerful technology becomes, the deeper our questions must become:
Where is technology ultimately taking humanity?
As artificial intelligence continues to extend human capabilities, will we still understand the true value and dignity of human life?
As civilization advances, will we still remember who is truly Lord?
It is at this significant moment that we gather in Phoenix.
And 2026 carries another historic significance.
It marks the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America.
Two hundred and fifty years ago, a nation began with bold aspirations concerning liberty, human dignity, and the future of society.

Over the generations, America has experienced war and peace, conflict and reconciliation, failure and renewal. Yet through its journey, the United States has also made significant contributions to the world through democracy, education, science and technology, medicine, humanitarian service, economic development, and global engagement.
For the global Church, there is another history worth remembering.
Generations of American Christians, churches, missionaries, educators, physicians, and humanitarian workers crossed the Pacific and came to Asia.
They established schools and hospitals.
They translated the Bible, trained leaders, planted churches, cared for the poor and vulnerable, and in many cases gave their entire lives serving people in lands far from home.
Many churches, educational institutions, medical ministries, and Christian movements across Asia today have been touched in some way by this legacy of faith and sacrifice.
Therefore, as we come to America in its 250th anniversary year, we come not only to attend another international gathering.
We come with gratitude.
We remember those who carried what they had received beyond their own borders.
We honor those who crossed the Pacific with faith, education, medicine, compassion, and the Gospel.
But an anniversary should never be only about remembering the achievements of the past.
It should also invite us to ask:
What will we leave to the next generation?

journeyStory.heading: From Receiving Blessings to Becoming a Blessing
paragraphs: For many generations, Asia was considered one of the great mission fields of the world.
Missionaries came from Europe and North America to Asia.
Today, the world is changing.
Asia has become one of the most significant regions shaping global population, economics, technology, culture, and innovation.
And the Asian Church is increasingly becoming an important mission force for the global Church.
This gives our journey to Phoenix in 2026 a deeper meaning.

In the past, we received many blessings.
Today, we are also called to become a blessing.
This is not about East replacing West.
It is not about one nation, culture, or Church becoming more important than another.
It is about entering a new season of partnership.
From one-way mission to mutual mission.
From giving and receiving to strengthening one another.
From Mission Field to Mission Force.
From the mission of individual nations to the shared mission of the Kingdom of God.
This is also at the heart of the vision of the Impact Asia Alliance.
We are not seeking to build another large organization.
Nor are we gathering simply to create another international conference.
We want to build a table.
A table where leaders from Asia, America, and nations around the world—across generations, cultures, professions, churches, and communities—can sit together and ask:
What is God doing in the world today?
And how can we participate together?

journeyStory.heading: From Digital Civilization to Eternal Governance
paragraphs: The theme of our 2026 Phoenix gathering is:
From Digital Civilization to Eternal Governance.
This gathering is not simply about artificial intelligence.
The deeper question is:
As technology reshapes civilization, how should Christians rediscover and live out our mission?
The mission field of the twenty-first century is no longer found only within the walls of the Church.
Business, education, technology, media, healthcare, government, the arts, culture, and the digital world are all shaping the next generation.
Therefore, the future of mission cannot depend only upon pastors and missionaries.
Entrepreneurs, educators, scientists, engineers, healthcare professionals, media leaders, artists, public leaders, and emerging innovators must also rediscover their calling.

Every believer has a calling.
Every workplace can become a mission field.
Every profession can become a platform for blessing the world.

Technology may help humanity move faster,
but faith must help us know where we are going.

Artificial intelligence may extend human capabilities,
but it cannot define human dignity.

Civilization may create increasingly powerful tools,
but truth, love, justice, and wisdom must determine what kind of world we are building.

journeyStory.heading: Why Phoenix?
paragraphs: And so, in 2026, we come to Phoenix.
We come to America.
We come to the desert.
Here, we look backward with gratitude and forward with hope.
We remember 250 years of the American journey, and we give thanks for the many ways this nation and generations of its people have contributed to and blessed the world.
But we also look toward a new chapter.
We hope that leaders from America, Asia, and nations around the world will meet here again—not simply to celebrate the past, but to discern our shared responsibility for the future.
In Scripture, the wilderness is never merely a place of emptiness.

It is often the place where people become quiet again.
Where they listen again.
Where they rediscover their calling.
And where they encounter God in unexpected ways.
In a world increasingly filled with information, algorithms, artificial intelligence, and countless competing voices, perhaps we need the wilderness again.
We need to rediscover the light that can truly guide humanity into the future.

Technology can change the world,
but only the Gospel can transform the human heart.

Artificial intelligence can extend human ability,
but only the Kingdom of God can reveal humanity's ultimate direction.
Therefore, the 2026 gathering in Phoenix is not an ending.
It is a new beginning.

We come to America with gratitude.
We cross the Pacific with friendship.
We bring generations together around one table.
And we leave again with a shared mission for the world.

In generations past, others crossed the Pacific and brought blessings to Asia.
Today, we cross the Pacific again and meet in Phoenix.

Not to replace one another.
Not to compete with one another.
But to stand together for the next generation—
and together, become a blessing to the world.

From Digital Civilization to Eternal Governance.
From Asia to the World.

From a light in the wilderness
to a shared mission for the next generation.
